\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضمان} (ḍamān)}{ضمان (ḍamān)}]{\ar{ضمان} (ḍamān) — a guarantee; a warranty}

\label{lesson:AR-C458-daman}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get cheaper, then the Arabic for to spend money.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضمان}}
\textbf{\ar{ضمان}} — \emph{ḍamān} — \textquotedblleft{}a guarantee; a warranty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{للجهاز} \ar{ضمان} \ar{لمدة} \ar{سنة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{li-l-jihāz ḍamān li-muddat sana.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The device has a one-year guarantee.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضمان}} (\emph{ḍamān}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-m-n}, \textquotedblleft{}to be answerable for\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍamān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍamān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-l-jihāz ḍamān li-muddat sana.} — The device has a one-year guarantee.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to get cheaper, then the Arabic for to spend money, then say \emph{ḍamān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ضمان} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A guarantee; a warranty\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سعر} (siʿr)}{سعر (siʿr)}]{\ar{سعر} (siʿr) — a rate; a price}

\label{lesson:AR-C458-sir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to spend money, then the Arabic for a guarantee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سعر}}
\textbf{\ar{سعر}} — \emph{siʿr} — \textquotedblleft{}a rate; a price\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سعر} \ar{الصرف} \ar{في} \ar{المطار} \ar{مرتفع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{siʿr aṣ-ṣarf fī al-maṭār murtafiʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The exchange rate at the airport is high.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أسعار}, \emph{asʿār}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سعر}} (\emph{siʿr}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-ʿ-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to kindle a fire\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives \emph{siʿr}, \textquotedblleft{}a price\textquotedblright{}, on the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siʿr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{siʿr aṣ-ṣarf fī al-maṭār murtafiʿ.} — The exchange rate at the airport is high.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to spend money, then the Arabic for a guarantee, then say \emph{siʿr} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سلعة} (silʿa)}{سلعة (silʿa)}]{\ar{سلعة} (silʿa) — a commodity; an item for sale}

\label{lesson:AR-C458-silaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a guarantee, then the Arabic for a rate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سلعة}}
\textbf{\ar{سلعة}} — \emph{silʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}a commodity; an item for sale\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{هذه} \ar{السلعة} \ar{رخيصة} \ar{في} \ar{السوق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hādhihi as-silʿa rakhīṣa fī as-sūq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This item is cheap at the market.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{سلع}, \emph{silaʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سلعة}} (\emph{silʿa}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{s-l-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}goods, merchandise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{silʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hādhihi as-silʿa rakhīṣa fī as-sūq.} — This item is cheap at the market.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a guarantee, then the Arabic for a rate, then say \emph{silʿa} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أرجع} (arjaʿa)}{أرجع (arjaʿa)}]{\ar{أرجع} (arjaʿa) — to take back; to return (something)}

\label{lesson:AR-C458-arjaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a rate, then the Arabic for a commodity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أرجع}}
\textbf{\ar{أرجع}} — \emph{arjaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to take back; to return (something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أرجعت} \ar{الحذاء} \ar{إلى} \ar{المتجر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{arjaʿtu al-ḥidhāʾ ilā al-matjar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I took the shoes back to the shop.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرجع}, \emph{yurjiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أرجع}} (\emph{arjaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-j-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to return\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to make go back\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a rate, then the Arabic for a commodity, then say \emph{arjaʿa} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قايض} (qāyaḍa)}{قايض (qāyaḍa)}]{\ar{قايض} (qāyaḍa) — to barter}

\label{lesson:AR-C458-qayada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a commodity, then the Arabic for to take back.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قايض}}
\textbf{\ar{قايض}} — \emph{qāyaḍa} — \textquotedblleft{}to barter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{قايض} \ar{المزارع} \ar{القمح} \ar{بالملح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qāyaḍa al-muzāriʿ al-qamḥ bi-l-milḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The farmer bartered the wheat for salt.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يقايض}, \emph{yuqāyiḍ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قايض}} (\emph{qāyaḍa}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{q-y-ḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}to give in exchange\textquotedblright{}. It is Form III.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
